output.reason: The evidence supports the first part of the claim: it states that penal charges for loans sanctioned to “individual borrowers, for purposes other than business” “shall not be higher than” penal charges applicable to non-individual borrowers for similar non-compliance. However, the second part is only partially supported: while the evidence says the specific circular ("Fair Lending Practice - Penal Charges in Loan Accounts (2023)") was withdrawn/repealed effective 2025-11-28 (so it is no longer in force as of 2026-11-23), it does not establish that the “corporate-comparison rule” is found only in the superseded circular (i.e., it could also appear elsewhere).
